units.summary: Root package.json overrides must not conflict with a direct dependency. An override of a direct dependency must use the `$<name>` reference or the identical spec, and every `$<name>` reference must name a direct dependency. Otherwise npm ci fails with EOVERRIDE.
units.evidence: package.json:41-43 (`"overrides": {"@nextcloud/files": "$@nextcloud/files"}`, where @nextcloud/files is a direct dependency at ^4.1.1); npm ci runs at .github/workflows/npm-build.yml:86, node-test.yml:84, lint-eslint.yml:82 and lint-stylelint.yml:78. The npm overrides rule comes from npm's package.json documentation; npm/arborist source was not available offline.
units.alint: needs: entry-values. It joins (override key, value) rows to (dependency name, spec) rows. The eventual assertion family is reference (a `$` reference resolves to a direct dependency) plus equality (a non-`$` override of a direct dependency equals its spec).
units.reason: R7: npm makes this static check over package.json when it loads the root manifest. It is not resolution semantics, so it is classified like the workspace:/catalog:/patch: reference units of earlier batches (jest-B01, jest-B03, tq-15, trpc-10). Batch-2 ruling: an assertion that joins a name to its value is B-adapter. A JSONPath filter cannot compare an override value with the dependency entry another key selects. Confidence: plausible. The exact EOVERRIDE conditions are recalled from npm documentation, not read from source. build/frontend-legacy's overrides are nested objects keyed by direct dependencies (@vitejs/plugin-vue2, @vueuse/integrations) and do not set those packages' own versions.

The same config's end-of-file-fixer hook is violated by 2669 tracked non-binary, non-empty files at the pin, including hand-edited ones: .editorconfig, 13 .sh, 6 .php and 2 .md. So neither contributors nor pre-commit.ci (which runs --all-files) apply these hooks. Stage A already excluded end-of-file-fixer for this reason (R5), and the reason applies equally to its sibling hooks in the same unused config. The rule can stay as value-add.

Global `respect_gitignore: false` is needed only for units 11, 12 and 13, but it widens the `**` scopes of units 15, 17 and 21 to ignored trees. Unit 07 fire test: Stage A injected Bamarni into autoload_psr4.php. The real script runs `composer dump-autoload` first, which regenerates that file from installed.json, so CI would pass that injection. The realistic break is a dev install committed into lib/composer/composer/installed.json. I reproduced that and the rule fires. The rule is stricter than the script for a stale autoload_* file whose installed.json lacks the plugin.

Unit 06: the rule excludes the root entry by `@.name != 'nextcloud'`, a value stand-in because JSONPath filters cannot test the "" member name. Renaming the root package fired the rule on scratch, a false positive. An entry with inBundle: true and no resolved/integrity fires, although npm records neither field for bundled packages; npm-package-lock-add-resolved's handling of such entries could not be checked offline, and the pin has none. `"resolved": ""` passes.

Unit 17 is partial, which is consistent with C. It does not cover reuse's bad-license check on LICENSES/ file stems that are neither SPDX ids nor LicenseRef-*. It also skips REUSE.toml `SPDX-License-Identifier = "..."` values, which Stage A notes. dist/*.map.license symlinks double-report a bad id in a sidecar.
Unit 20: the regex `^[^.]+.*\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$` fires on a dotfile such as LICENSES/.x.txt, which reuse would accept because it checks the suffix. This is an edge case.

Unit 15 covers only the example U+FFFD. The AGENTS.md convention is 'malformed or garbled characters', which also includes invalid UTF-8 and mojibake. The convention is addressed to coding agents, not human contributors.

Unit 12 copies $expectedFiles into the config, and the copy will drift. cross_file `relation: registered` with source.files '*', register_as '{basename}' and a regex target over build/files-checker.php reads the real array. It passes on the clone and fired on a new root file and a new root directory on scratch, but its regex depends on the array's layout.

Enforcement note: autocheckers.yml's paths filter (src: workflows, 3rdparty, **/appinfo, **/lib, **/templates, vendor-bin, composer.*, **.php) skips the translation and triple-dot checkers on PRs that change only l10n, .tx/config or JS/Vue. Transifex pushes are not checked either, so enforcement lags until the next PHP PR.

I could not reproduce Stage A's count of '4611 files' violating end-of-file-fixer: I count 2669 tracked non-binary, non-empty files that do not end in exactly one newline. The conclusion is unchanged.
stage_b_summary:
Mostly confirmed: Stage A missed two units, and I recommend removing two, reclassifying three and fixing four rules. validate-config loads 32 rules. `alint check` on the clone exits 0 with one finding, at info level: the value-add rule on lib/l10n/vi.json:34. On my own scratch copy I re-ran the fire tests for every A unit in the locale and dep-version families. Unit 01 fired on 6 breaks (l10n directory removed, the files, settings-1, dashboard-shipped-with-server and files_encryption resources each removed, a new app without a resource). Unit 02 fired on U+200F, U+0623 and U+206D in de/fr catalogs and stayed silent for ar.json, a character at line start and .js twins. Unit 04 fired on .js, .php n(), .vue and CRLF files and stayed silent for .map files and a call at line start. Unit 06 fired with resolved or integrity removed and stayed silent for a link entry. Unit 07 fired with the plugin in installed.json. I also sanity-checked units 03, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17 and 20. All broken copies fired as expected, and the clone passes. There is no toolchain-pin A unit, and I found no missed toolchain-pin gate: no .nvmrc, .tool-versions, .npmrc engine-strict or devEngines; CI reads root engines; PHP versions are hard-coded per workflow.

Missed units: (b01, A, other) every shipped app has composer/composer.json, because autoloaderchecker.sh's `composer i --no-dev -d apps/<app>/composer || exit 1` fails otherwise; the earlier batches counted such preconditions (signal-desktop-11). (b02, B-adapter, dep-version, needs entry-values) npm's overrides rule on the root package.json's `$@nextcloud/files`, enforced by npm ci; plausible, from npm docs.

Reclassify: unit 06's family to other (precedent signal-desktop-41). Units 18 and 19 from B-config to B-adapter: compound SPDX expressions exist at the pin, so they need an SPDX-expression extractor, and the LICENSES/ side is a directory listing.

Remove: units 21 and 22. The opt-in pre-commit config is not run in CI or mentioned in any doc, and its end-of-file-fixer hook is violated by 2669 tracked files.

Config problems: units 01 and 14 pass silently when .tx/config or psalm.xml is deleted, and they miss a stray file under apps/. The global respect_gitignore: false makes the rules for units 15, 17 and 21 scan node_modules. The autoloaderchecker.sh line citations for units 07, 10 and 28 point past the end of the 82-line file. Unit 07's fire test broke a file that composer regenerates, so CI would not have caught it. Unit 06 excludes the root entry by the root package's name, which gives a false positive if the package is renamed.

With these changes there are 53 units: A=11, C=7, B-config=0, B-adapter=5, D=30. That makes coverage_today 11/23, about 48% (from 43%); coverage_with_tuning 18/23, about 78%; gap 5/23, about 22%. The after-slice figure is unchanged because no B-config unit is left. By family: locale 3A/1C/1D; dep-version 1A/1B-adapter/2D; toolchain-pin 1D. I did not verify offline the source of npm-package-lock-add-resolved, npm/arborist or patch-package. A patch-package check (build/frontend-legacy/patches must target an installed package) was considered and not added: it is part of the D unit 08 (npm ci), and there is one patch at the pin.
notes: Counts: 53 units, A=10 (01, 02, 04, 06, 07, 11, 12, 14, 15, 20), C=8 (03, 13, 17, 21, 23, 24, 26, 27), B-config=2 (18 reference, 19 set), B-adapter=3 (16, 22, 25), B-kernel=0, B-delegate=0, D=30. coverage_today=10/23 (about 43%), coverage_with_tuning=18/23 (about 78%), gap=5/23 (about 22%). Neither B-config unit uses equality, unique-key or cardinality, so the after-slice figure is unchanged. Per family: locale 3A/1C/0B/1D; dep-version 2A/0B/2D; toolchain-pin 1D only (no addressable toolchain-pin unit); other is the rest. R4 fire tests for every A unit in locale and dep-version ran on scratch copies under <scratch>/nextcloud-server-a; each fired when broken and passed on the clean copy and on the clone. Extra sanity fires on a second scratch tree also confirmed the htaccess, unexpected root file and directory, expected-present, psalm, bad SPDX id, license without extension, broken YAML and U+FFFD rules. The scratch directory has been removed. Caveats: (a) npm-package-lock-add-resolved@1.1.4's source was not read offline, so unit 06 treating a missing integrity like a missing resolved is inferred from its purpose and not verified. (b) In the commented-out nextcloud-23 rule, the conventional-commit type list is an approximation; webiny/action-conventional-commits' own list was not read. (c) psalm-checker.sh skips git-ignored app dirs, but the alint rule (with respect_gitignore: false) would also see untracked, ignored apps in a developer checkout. On a CI checkout the two are identical. (d) The DCO sign-off (unit 26) is enforced by the organization's DCO app, outside the repo, and is recorded from docs only. (e) Units 23, 24, 26 and 27 are git-history C rules left commented out in the config, because the clone is depth 1. (f) Not counted as units: the masked JSON-parse check, the debug-only en_GB check, end-of-file-fixer (violated by 4611 files, R5), pre-commit php-lint and php-cs-fixer (collapsed into 30 and 31), npm-build.yml's commented-out recompile check, PR-template checklist items, and the PHP floor, engines and app-version coherence (value-add only). No spawning kinds, custom facts or active git-history kinds are used. The clone was not modified (git status clean).

changes.detail: file_exists .tx/config. Closes Stage B's R4 gap: when .tx/config is missing, translation-checker.php:15 reads false and str_contains at :67 throws a TypeError. Reproduced the gap: with .tx/config deleted on scratch, nextcloud-l10n-app-in-tx-config still reports 0 findings. Fire test: the new rule fires (1 finding, <repo>) with .tx/config deleted, is silent on the clean scratch copy, and passes on the clone.

file_absent apps/*. translation-checker.php:60-70 walks apps/ with DirectoryIterator and treats every entry as an app. psalm-checker.sh:8-17 does the same with `for app in apps/*` for a tracked file. Reproduced the gap: nextcloud-l10n-app-has-l10n-dir stays silent with apps/README.md added. Fire test: fires on apps/README.md and on apps/.DS_Store, silent on the clean scratch copy. apps/ holds only the 34 app directories at the pin, so the clone passes.
file_exists psalm.xml. Without psalm.xml the grep at psalm-checker.sh:14 fails for every app. Fire test: fires with psalm.xml deleted on scratch, silent on the clean copy, passes on the clone.

Stage B's missed unit (A, other): for_each_dir over apps/* requiring file_exists {path}/composer/composer.json. Checked in the clone that all 34 app dirs have composer/composer.json, and that autoloaderchecker.sh:53 runs `composer i --no-dev -d ${app}/composer || exit 1` for every non-ignored directory. Fire test: fires on apps/dav after removing its composer/composer.json, fires on a new apps/newapp with no composer dir, silent on the clean copy, passes on the clone. Comment notes the same dev-checkout caveat as unit 14: the script skips gitignored apps, the rule does not.

Moved to family other (Stage B; precedent signal-desktop-41). Root exclusion changed from `@.name != 'nextcloud'` to `@.name != $.name`, which no longer depends on the package name. Verified that $.name is evaluated: changing only packages[""].name makes the rule fire. Fire test on a scratch copy of package-lock.json: renaming the package in both places is now silent (it was a false positive), dropping resolved fires, dropping integrity fires, dropping resolved from an alias entry fires, and a link entry missing both is silent. The clean copy and the clone pass. Comment records two things not verified offline: how the action treats inBundle entries, and an empty-string resolved.

Evidence corrected to build/autoloaderchecker.sh:35-42 (dump-autoload :35, Bamarni grep :37-42); the file has 82 lines. Scope now excludes lib/composer/composer/autoload_*.php, because dump-autoload rewrites those files before the grep, so CI would pass a stale one (the classmap diff at :59-82 looks only at autoload_classmap). Fire test on a scratch copy of lib/composer/composer: fires on a dev-mode installed.json carrying the bamarni plugin's Bamarni\\Composer\\Bin psr-4 entry, fires on Bamarni injected into installed.php, and is now silent on Bamarni injected only into autoload_psr4.php (matching CI). The clean copy and the clone pass. Unit records 10 and 28 also cite out-of-range lines. The correct ones are composer download :8-17, version guard :20-28, per-app loop :44-57 and classmap diff :59-82. Those are Stage A unit records, not config, so they are not edited here.

Regex changed from ^[^.]+.*\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$ to ^.+\.[^.]+$, which follows Python's Path.suffix. The suffix is non-empty only when the last '.' comes after the first character and before the last one. Fire test on a scratch copy of LICENSES/: fires on LICENSES/MIT, LICENSES/MIT. and LICENSES/.MIT. It is silent on LICENSES/.x.txt (Stage B's false positive, fixed) and on LICENSES/GPL-3.0, whose suffix is '.0'. The clean copy and the clone pass.

Scope now excludes the gitignored trees: **/node_modules/**, vendor-bin/**/vendor/**, lib/composer/bin/**, lib/composer/bamarni/**, data/**, build/lib/**, build/bin/**, updater/** and apps?*/**. This fixes Stage B's respect_gitignore widening. Comment notes the rule covers only U+FFFD, not invalid UTF-8 or mojibake. Fire test: fires on U+FFFD appended to lib/public/IUser.php and to apps/dav/composer/composer.json, which shows apps?*/** does not exclude apps/. It is silent on U+FFFD under node_modules/, build/frontend/node_modules/, vendor-bin/cs-fixer/vendor/, apps-extra/ and data/. The clean copy and the clone pass.

C. Same gitignored-tree excludes as unit 15. The comment now lists the partial coverage: REUSE.toml TOML values are not checked; LICENSES/ stems that are neither SPDX ids nor LicenseRef-* are not checked; and a bad id in a sidecar is reported again through each dist/*.map.license symlink. Passes on the clone. Fires on 'AGPL-3.0-onlyy' in lib/public/IUser.php and on a deprecated GPL-2.0 in build/frontend/src/a.js. Silent on a bad id under node_modules/ and apps-extra/.

Stage B removed the unit: the opt-in pre-commit config is run by no workflow and asked for by no doc (grep of *.md and *.yml found no reference). The rule keeps its id, moves to the VALUE-ADD section at level info, and its comment names both limitations: not enforced, and alint's reader is more lenient than check-yaml. It also gets the gitignored-tree excludes. Passes on the clone. Fires (resource_parse analysis failure) on a broken .github/workflows/reuse.yml. Silent on a broken YAML under node_modules/.

Stage B removed the unit (same opt-in pre-commit config). It had no rule. The header moves it out of NOT EXPRESSIBLE into a NOT ENFORCED note covering all three pre-commit hooks. They need an SPDX-expression extractor, because compound expressions such as 'AGPL-3.0-or-later AND MIT' and REUSE.toml's 'CC-BY-SA-3.0 OR GPL-3.0-or-later' must be split into ids. Not a reproduced defect, so the rules are unchanged. The comment names the drift risk and why the drift-free registered-relation form was not used: its regex depends on the array's layout, which makes it C.

The workflow runs on pull_request only, so pushes are not checked. Enforcement therefore lags; no bucket change.
